Also, it was difficult to apply another layer. The tip was dry so it would actually scratch off parts of the eyeliner, causing patches.

The eyeliner cannot be rubbed off easily which is really nice. However, scratching it with a nail does scratch off easily, so as long as you don’t do that or scrape it with the brush itself, it will stay put pretty well.

Update: Since I didn’t want to give up on it completely & waste money spent on this one already, I found a way to make it work. If the tip of the brush becomes dry, I lightly twirl the tip of the brush on the top of my hand until the liquid appears. Then I apply on my eyelid until it gets dry again. This process has to be repeated unfortunately, but I really do like the minimalist look the eyeliner can create and how it stays on even after work out & being outside in the day during the summer.

I was very excited about this razor based on the glowing reviews. I really wanted to love it- and there is indeed a lot to like about it. It's good but not great and probably not super beginner friendly as the heft makes it more aggressive and less forgiving.

The head looks like a copy of the Edwin Jagger DE89 or Muhle R89. The blade gap is a bit more aggressive than either of those razors. It also appears a bit more aggressive than the medium setting of my adjustable razors. The construction and fit and finish are decent but not especially stellar. It is made well enough that the blade is easy to load and center- and the blade stays very secure with proper alignment. This is very important and it's definitely there.

The knurling on the handle is good- but the edges did feel a bit sharp/rough which made it seem a bit cheap. It is a VERY hefty handle. By far the heaviest I've used. I thought this would be a good thing but it makes the razor seem a bit unbalanced and perhaps even a bit more aggressive than the head otherwise would be. It also makes the razor less conducive to finer, shorter moments like blade buffing and more likely to cause razor burn if not careful. It is a good combination- but for me it works best for a quick, reasonably efficient 2 pass shave. I feel like it is a bit too much and too unwieldily for a 3rd pass against the grain.

This is a good razor -but it may not be a perfect fit for many. You should also consider that this razor has been selling around $16-18 and around the $17+ price point there are a lot of other very solid options. If you compare it to other budget friendly options like sub $18 West Coast Shaving's stainless steel razors, or similarly priced Vikings Cheiftain Jr., or a real DE89 which is sometimes seen under $22 here on Amazon- I'm not sure this is the amazing bargain that others are portraying in the reviews.

Some have compared it to $40+ Merkurs, etc. It's kind of a weird comparison. True this is a very functional and solid razor - and Merkurs are overpriced due to the name and legacy. But those are also different razors - i.e. milder with lighter more refined handles for finer control, and built a bit better. The razor has to be right for you before you can compare price. If a razor is unbalanced and clunky (or not) - that's part of the design you're paying for. It's not just about how good the chrome job is.

If you know what you're getting into you'll enjoy this solid razor at a reasonable price. Just don't expect a superior razor selling for 1/2 or 1/3 the price of the name brand competition as others may claim here.

A plastic jar full of lavender-colored and -scented bath salts. (Apparently some of my Pre De Provence products are showing up in one review - so while this reveiw is for bath salts, I have the lavender lotion as well, which I do love the scent of it but as with the bath salts, wish the bottle were nicer).

There was no seal on the top of the jar, just the lid. That's fine, but I would wonder how long it would sit on a shelf before purchasing and how "fresh" the scent would last. I sprinkled some in my bathroom sink that I'd filled with warm water. The water turned a slight lavender shade as the bath salts turned clear. The salt crystals did melt pretty quickly, though as with any bath salts I've used there are always a few that are stubborn.

I did think it a bit pricey at just under $17 (at time of this review). For that price, I'd like a glass bottle or something prettier in the jar design itself, though the lavender-colored crystals do look pretty. Something that made it attractive to me, and that would be a pretty bottle/jar that I could display in my bathroom in my basket of bath goodies. Or, to give someone as a gift.

This plastic jar makes it seem like one of those cheaper jars of bath salts you can buy at Big Lots, which I can do for less than half the price if I want bath salts. Pretty it up some so I feel I'm getting my money's worth. You cold say Pre De Provence has quality ingredients and maybe that's why the price, but I'm not finding it special enough to pay almost $17.

This comes in a nice outer product box. Made in Korea. The brand’s website said it’s 100% vegan, excluding animal ingredients and animal experiments. It also doesn’t include parabens.

It comes in a nice compact. It’s a compact like a cushion foundation where you open it and there’s a kind of lid that holds the sponge applicator, and you lift that lid to reveal the product. You press the applicator sponge into it (or your own sponge or brush) and then apply it. The brand’s website said the included sponge applicator is an “eco puff” made of “eco-friendly corns” and is “99.9% anti-bacterial and water-repellent,” which makes it safe on skin and keeps puff clean.

This is a liquidy but balm kind of texture. It isn’t as thick as a balm. It just feels like a cushion foundation. But this isn’t a foundation. It has a very light, mint green color to it. It’s so light that it’s almost white but has the green color to it. When applied, it reduces redness. It doesn’t do as well as my more pigmented green correctors, but it does a nice job while being hydrating and lightweight on the skin. It’s something that works well before applying foundation. It is lightweight enough to wear well under foundation. It isn’t a primer really, it doesn’t smooth out the skin or fill in pores. But, it does reduce the redness in my skin so then I use less foundation and concealer. If you have a TON of redness or it’s REALLY red, this might not be enough since it isn’t extremely pigmented. But, it will make a difference. I like it isn’t drying on the skin either.

I’m just not sure how I feel about it though. It works well on the skin. But, I do like to know what’s in my products. I don’t like that they provided barely any product info, and the ingredients on the product box weren’t in English. They also didn’t include them here on the product page. Not even the product photos provided any real info on the product - what it does, who it’s for, how to use it, ingredients, etc. I had to go to the brand’s website to find out more. Yes, it’s a simple Google search, but it’s not really something you should have to do.

Normally, I would just go to the brand’s website to find the list of ingredients when they’re not included on the Amazon product page. But, the Jung Saem Mool website didn’t have them on their website either. I looked for them elsewhere and did find an ingredient list on Korean Beauty Box, but didn’t think they were accurate because they didn’t include centella asiatica, pine sprout, or green calamine powder, which are supposed to be in this product. So, I translated the ingredients from the box myself. But, I’m not that confident in the ingredients provided on the box.(I included a photo from the box, and also included the ingredients at the end of my review in English)

It doesn’t seem like a complete list of ingredients to me. It has the first ingredient as titanium dioxide. It has tocopherol (vitamin E) as the 3rd ingredient. The rest of the ingredient are 7, kind of versions I’d guess you’d call them, of centella asiatica. There’s nothing else listed. It’s kind of odd. The brand’s website said this is supposed to have “2 plants - pine sprout containing fresh moisture and centella asiatica roots.” I saw the “centella asiatica roots” in the ingredients when I translated them. But didn’t see any “pine sprout.” I also saw something about “cica pine water” on the brand’s website, but again, not sure what that’s supposed to be? The brand’s website also mentioned “Natural green calamine powder covers reddened skin tone.” Again, I didn’t see any calamine powder at all in the ingredients.

The 7, I guess versions, of Centella Asiatica are:
Centella Asiatica Extract (5,159,235ppm) - Well known soothing, antioxidant, and moisturizing ingredient. Anti-inflammatory. The main biologically active components are Asiaticoside, madecassoside, asiatic acid, and madecassic acid. All of which are in this.

Centella Asiatica Leaf Extract (0.035ppm)

Centella Asiatica Root Extract (0.03ppm)

Madecassoside (0.0025ppm) - One of the main biologically active components of Centella Asiatica.

Madecassic Acid (0.0025ppm) - One of the main biologically active components of Centella Asiatica.

Asiaticoside (0.0025ppm) - One of the main biologically active components of Centella Asiatica.

Asiatic Acid (0.0025ppm) - One of the main biologically active components of Centella Asiatica. It’s less prominent than it’s sister component, Asiaticoside, but it still contributes to the well-established moisturizing and wound healing abilities of Centella Asiatica.

Overall, it works well. It reduces my redness, feels hydrating on the skin, and works well on its own and under foundation. It feels lightweight on the skin. If they provided the full ingredient list, it would be something I’d be willing to purchase. But, right now, I don’t like they didn’t include them and don’t like that they can’t even be found online as far as I could tell. And I just have a hard time believing the ingredient list I translated from the box is the full ingredient list. I don’t know. If the ingredients aren’t a big factor for you, this is nice and works well. If knowing the ingredients are important to you, I’d look elsewhere. There’s other similar products that actually provide a full ingredient list, and a lot of them are far cheaper. I give it 3 stars.

Use as last step of skin care routine. Dip puff into content and gently apply and dab on skin.

The clear stamper came just as described. I haven't actually used it on my nails yet but I have played around with it on some paper and it picks up the images perfectly. After reading some concerning reviews on other clear stampers I was hesitant to purchase this one. However, I have had no problems as of yet. The only flaw is that there are two little dent/scratches on the stamper head and I am afraid eventually it will lead to bigger dents/scratches. With it being so inexpensive I wouldn't mind purchasing another one for back-up, just in case. I do not use any scrapers that come with the stampers, as I use gift cards because they are much easier to use and swipe with.

The stamper head is squishy but not marshmallow squishy. It is possible to squish on your nail without rolling, so long as you do not have extremely wide nail beds. It is a little hard to get used to being able to see through and it takes some practice getting it lined up exactly where you want, but it's easier once you do it a few times. As I stated earlier, the images are very crisp and clean when being picked up. Instead of squishing down like I did with my other stamper I instead try to roll/flick the stamper across. This is more for the fear of damaging the stamper, as I've read about others who did not have success with clear stampers.

Make sure that when you use it you do not clean it with acetone/polish remover as it will eventually make the stamper head cloudy and no longer see through. Also, do not buff or anything before first use, I found that it picks up perfectly without having to do any of that.

I highly recommend getting this stamper if you love to stamp but have problems with perfect placing, such as myself.

I am one of those few people that is cursed with very fine hair that becomes oily/greasy if I do not wash it daily. I tend to avoid hair products that contain the word oil in the product description as I do not need any help in it becoming oily. I also do not use conditioner regularly due to the nature of my hair.
My first thoughts upon opening my package of the InstaNatural Argan Oil Shampoo, was that it was well protected by the quality seals. There is a thin plastic cover over the bottle to prevent leakage during shipment, and another quality seal that you have to remove by taking off the top of the bottle. The first thing I do when I go to buy or use a new shampoo is to smell it. When ordering hair products online, you do not get to smell before you buy and have to depend on the seller or reviews for a description of the scent. The scent of this shampoo is a clean scent. It is mild and not overwhelming. It is not a perfume smell or a fruity smell. The best way I can describe it is a nice clean mild smell.
I started with hair that had been washed the day before, so it was oily and ready for another wash. I wet my hair and applied about a quarter size amount to my hair. I have shoulder length hair, so I do not need much. This shampoo has an amazing lather to it. It is thick and you can really feel it working through your hair. I scrubbed it in from the scalp to the ends. Then I rinsed. I am one of those that needs to feel/hear the squeak when I am rinsing to know my hair is really clean. And this shampoo passed that test very well. I did not use any conditioner afterwards, because I do not normally, unless it is a weekly treatment.
I usually air dry my hair, and I did this time as well. My hair came out so soft and full of body and did not have any heavy feeling to it. I woke up this morning without the greasy/oily feel I usually get the next day after I wash. I was very surprised by this, because like I said that is normally what my hair feels like unless I wash it daily. It is still soft and feels silky to the touch.
I had my fiance do the sniff test to see what he thought of the smell, and he said it smelled nice.
If you are like me and have been avoiding any shampoos because of the description having oil in it, I would say to give this one a try. It is like a clarifying shampoo with just the right amount to give your hair the softness that it needs without weighing it down.

UPDATE! The Shrinking Packages of hair

BEFORE
In my last review, I commented that at the beginning, I was pleased with the price and that the amount of hair matched the pictures. Over time however, I found that:
1) the packaging changed from “factory original “ (like the clear plastic sleeves like you see braids come in) to ziplock bags (like you put your kid’s lunch in). Not cool, but not bad.
2) After the packaging change, I started to notice that each time I bought the hair, there was less and less hair in the little ziplock baggies. Definitely NOT cool and super BAD :-/

NOW!!!
Flyteng responded my review by suggesting I give them another try (no extra hair or admission of the skimping however). I did because the price was still great at a bit over 15 bucks and my hair did look really cute (for a little while at least- more later).

For the last three purchases, there has been more hair in the bags. V. Cool. Still in ziplocks though. Ratchet. The price has gone up close to 3 bucks, but at least the the amounts of hair are more consistent.

The Hair
It looks beautiful and natural for about a week. It’s soft and feels light and great. Something happens into the second week however and the hair starts to get hard and really nappy. Now full disclosure: when I install, I pull a lot of the coils apart. When I do this, it looks absolutely natural (I joined a Black Girl Magic Meet up - they ALL that it was mine and you know we know). Since I don’t mind nappy hair, it’s cool. I do have to cut the matted ends daily to not look like I haven’t been lost in the desert for a month, but again, I’m cool with that.

All in all, I would say that I will continue to use it as long as:
1) the price doesn’t continue to go up (might have to do with China tariffs - anybody else feeling this our hair products?).
2) they don’t start back skimping on the hair.

Happy Crocheting Y’all!!

I've been a natural deodorant user for years and have tried many brands on the market, my favorite so far has been Native, which is also one of the most popular, so I thought I would do a comparison with that brand.

Both are stick deodorants, but the PF deodorant has a larger case, and just a little more product, barely enough worth mentioning though. The deodorant on the PF brand slides on thicker and isn't as hard as the Native deodorant so it would be easier to apply too much with the PF than with Native. Not huge but something to consider.

They both seem to do an equally good job at keeping odor away and I noticed no increase in odor while wearing the PF vs. the Native.

Price-wise they are about the same so you really don't save money either way.

Fragrance-wise I didn't really have a preference for one brand vs. the other, they both have a nice range of fragrance and there is enough variety to appeal to most people.

Because of application, I will be sticking with Native, but if you are looking for something that glides on a bit thicker than this would be the best choice.

Like the hair on my head, my eyelashes are thin and fine. Without mascara, they are barely noticeable. I have never before tried an eyelash growth serum and was frankly somewhat skeptical, yet at the same time, I was excited at the thought that this product might be beneficial.

This serum is packaged in a tube that looks like mascara. However, the inner wand ends in a tiny brush that is like a VERY thin paintbrush. I would have preferred a slightly thicker applicator; the brush was SO small that it was difficult to see the serum for precise application.

I followed the instructions for this product, applying nightly along my lash line. I used this product daily for over a month (since late August). Unfortunately, I am not able to discern any noticeable results. I actually took photos, thinking that might show more of a difference, I but do not see any changes in the photos, either. (It looks like Amazon has finally posted my photos, so you can see what you think for yourself.)

The only small improvement I have noticed of late is that AFTER applying my mascara, my lashes seem longer than they normally would with mascara--it's almost as if they are somehow adhering to the mascara better than they would normally. I'm not 100% sure if this is a real effect, but that possible sign combined with the fact that I didn't have any adverse reactions to this product is the reason why I gave it two stars rather than one. Perhaps others will have better luck than I did.

UPDATED 11/9/14: Despite my lack of results after one month, I continued to use this product. It has now been over two months, and I believe that I have seen SOME results. At this point, my lashes DO appear longer--I think that's why my mascara has seemed to be working better, as my lashes are a bit longer than before. However, my results have been nothing like the miracles in the photos posted on the product page--yes, my lashes are a bit longer, but the effect is hardly noticeable to the bare eye (I asked my husband, and he didn't notice). Furthermore, my lashes are neither thicker nor more plentiful; this product gave me a bit of length only, not thickness or any other effect. So, in summary, I upgraded my review from two to three stars, but I don't feel like I can go beyond that at this time.

I never suspected I would be writing a review about what appears to be a sander to use on ones feet but here I am doing exactly that.
About 18-20 months ago my husband who has adult onset diabetes injured his large toe. He was on a job site and accidentally tripped over something but because of advanced diabetes he has neuropathy which has caused him to lose most sensation in his feet. I discovered the injury as he was putting on his socks and when I began to put medication and a bandage on his toe, the end of the toe nearly fell off in my hand. So needless to say a long complicated process began to save his toe; possibly his entire foot.
As we age our feet do too. We may get thick calluses which can crack deep into the layers of the skin that are very painful and make the feet susceptible to infection, an infection that can easily become a long standing crisis not just for a diabetic but for everybody when their feet begin to misbehave. Yes, even you! Believe it or not we are still trying to get his feet to heal. Foot Cream of every kind in the house, epsom salt foot soaks, special socks and shoes. Bandaids come in more shapes, sizes and uses than one can imagine. Sports tape, implements to grind the callus down before they crack, and on and on until one wants to pull their hair out. Your entire life focus revolves around diabetic care! I can honestly say that until this happened I had never given a thought to diabetes and now it is all I think of or so it seems.
So at this point, I was frustrated, frightened and more than a little angry. I finally purchased a rasp and used it to sand the calluses on my husbands feet. At the same time I was having my own problems with my feet but had no idea that my feet were going thru the same thing. Ouch!
Now I was really getting worried because the rasp was just not effective enough to get this stuff under control and I didn't know what to do when a strange thing happened. I purchased a Dremel tool to help with some heavy cleaning I needed to do and as I used it, it occurred to me that something like this could be beneficial for the foot problem if it wasn't so dangerous.
That thought as most of mine do eventually deserted me but one day I was browsing Amazon for foot care and I saw what appeared to be a Dremel and initially thought my page had flipped. But I was intrigued so I decided to compare it to mine and that is when I discovered it is a foot Dremel! What? No! Really? Yep, a foot Dremel. Well I guess you know I spent hours on Amazon reviewing these things and this product had so many outstanding reviews I decided to give it a try.
What a blessed relief this little tool has become, a virtual life saver. I read the instructions because there is an appropriate way to have good foot hygiene and by this time I wanted nothing less than the best. We immediately began foot baths with a little Apple Cider Vinegar, sometimes Epsom Salts, or Hydrogen Peroxide, anything safe to help soften the calluses. Then I turned on my foot dremel and OMG! Once I practiced how to use it without causing further damage it was as if a miracle had occurred. The deep fissures in his feet are healing fast enough that more aren't developing and the tool is has a small surface so I used it on the toe that he had injured. We thought that toe had healed and were focusing on the calluses by then. Anyway a callus had developed on the toe but it looked OK. Well, there is ok and then there is OK! As the callus began to disappear I could see flecks of red so I felt bad because I thought I had been careless with the tool. The second time I used it on the toe which was red and painful by now three pin point holes began to bleed. Suddenly I began to realize that those were the place his toe nearly fell off. The infection had never healed! The wound had sealed over for all of that time just waiting, a spectre of death stalking my husband!
Within 3-4 days the redness around his toenail began to ease and the holes are still open but now they can heal from the inside out. Such relief! Such gratitude washed over me because if that infection had been allowed to brood much longer it may have flooded his entire body with infection, life threatening infection!
I know this is a long story but I wanted to share this journey to instill the importance of foot hygiene whether you have diabetes or not yet....? One does not wait until their feet are in crisis mode before beginning good self care, which includes and instrument such as this. When you think you need it, you are likely wishing you already had one.
So, good proactive foot hygiene, a foot dremel (my words) something adequate to do foot soaks and appropriate things to aid in softening the calluses before they form deep painful fissures and the will to see it thru.
The reason I chose this particular instrument is because of the great reviews. Many items receive good reviews but when you look at the number of the reviews and they are consistently good with far less negative ones it is a good indicator that the item is at least worth a try so watch the numbers. They can indicate good but if there is just a few reviews VS lots of reviews then you know you are likely safe.
I highly recommend this item for yourself, gifts for the hard to shop for person and encourage you to educate yourselves on what foot hygiene consists of and begin it as a preventative measure then encourage your loved ones too.

When I try out a new electric toothbrush, I test it by using disclosing tablets. Using them, you can see the plaque on your teeth, and measure how much your brush leaves behind. This brush removed absolutely nothing. It's exactly like a standard manual toothbrush that buzzes.

The bristles on sonic toothbrushes vibrate in an up and down motion at high speed. They don't move far, but the speed they're traveling at allows them to scrub the surfaces of your teeth very efficiently. My old Sonicare (purchased before Philips bought them out) left NO plaque film behind.

Curious about the Oral-B's non-effectiveness, I held the bristles lightly against my tongue, and could feel no motion whatever. It's as though the handle vibrates, but the bristles remain stationary.

Fortunately, the brush is inexpensive, so I won't feel too bad about throwing it in the trash.

Second this brush does have quite of bit of weight to it and I found the handle start digging into my hand and causing some pain when I was trying to work through some knots in my hair.

That being said I was happy with the results, in my pictures the left size of my head was brushed with my old brush and the right side with this brush and I could see a visible different in the amount of frizzing my hair was doing, especially at the top.

As a female with significant hirsutism, I've been looking for a good facial epilator that won't take me a week to do the job. This is not it. It might be it if I planned to let my beard grow in for a week before epilating, but I'm not going to do that. Additionally, when I purchased this, I expected to have the whole epilator for my face. That's what I need--a wide path of hair-yankin' madness. The instructions for this say that the user should only use half of the epilator on the face and that the device removes "individual hairs" on the face when maneuvered this way. Honestly, I feel the description online was very lacking if that's the deal. Being frustrated with this situation after waiting for a week for the device, it should come as no surprise that I carefully used both opposing heads on my face exactly the way the instructions told me not to immediately after reading them. I still found myself pretty disappointed with the device's performance on my chin. For reasons that I have yet to understand, however, this device did do a pretty good job on my mustache and on my leg. Unfortunately, I bought it for my chin. Now I have three epilators. Each one does one thing fairly well. I just line 'em up and switch to the next when one gets hot. I'm thinking that I really only need two more parts of my face to be hair-free, so, if I pick just the right devices, my final arsenal will consist of five epilators--not for my whole body, mind you, but simply to epilate my face. I'm afraid the e60's greatest asset outside of ripping out lip hair with reasonable efficiency is that its small size means it takes up less space in my bathroom than I expected it to. If I have to have five of these, smaller is suddenly worth mentioning.
In all reality, this device has another important positive trait: I was pleasantly surprised by the pain level associated with it. I honestly did not believe that an epilator design could minimize the pain of yanking hair out by the root, but I was incorrect. I wish this thing worked better for the purpose I purchased it for because I have never had a more comfortable epilating experience.

I had severe scalp problems for the last several years. I grew up using ordinary commercial shampoo, but in my 40s I thought I was losing hair by my temples. On advice, I switched to a shampoo that promotes a healthy hair-growing environment. That helped a little for a few years, but eventually stopped doing even the little good it did.

I switched to herbal shampoos. Hooray for natural products, right? No, not right. I tried 8-10 of them. I developed horrible scalp problems (red, peeling, itchy). I tried rotating the shampoos, which was a little help, but not much. Finally, I thought that since I'm allergic to some plants, perhaps some of the herbal ingredients were causing my problems.

I switched to Sweet Baby Shampoo and had immediate relief. It is wonderful. I know some reviewers had problems with it, but guess what? Each individual is different! Wow, what a stunning thought! The glorified natural ingredients harmed me. The ingredients in Sweet Baby Shampoo help me.

I love Sweet Baby Shampoo. It is gentle and cleans well. For the first time in my life, I don't need so-called conditioner afterward. I can comb my hair right after washing it (although I don't). I would recommend it to anyone. But be sensible. Know your body's reactions and don't use anything that hurts you, and don't think of reviewers as experts.

Oh, one last thought. It's slow, but my hair seems to be growing back. It's too soon to guess how it will turn out because I've been using Sweet Baby for only 2-3 weeks. If I remember, I'll update about the hair regrowth.

These come in a nice little box. They are vegan and cruelty free. They are made in the USA. I included the ingredients at the end of my review.

You get 3 glosses - a peachy pink toned one that has a strawberry scent/flavor, a more reddish toned one that has a grape scent/flavor, and a clear one that has a bubble gum scent/flavor. As for the scents, I can notice them when applying, not so much after the fact. I don’t really notice a taste really with any of them, but the ingredients do list “flavor” not fragrance/parfum, so it made me think they’d have more taste to them. Not a big deal to me though.

While 2 of them are tinted in color, the color doesn’t really translate onto the lips. They just look clear on the lips. They don’t change any color of lip liner, lipstick, matte lip, etc. that I put them over top of. So, I liked that.

The formula is nice. It feels nice and moisturizing on the lips, which I expected given they have nice moisturizing ingredients like Shea butter, coconut oil, and squalane. They do feel SLIGHTLY sticky on the lips. I hate sticky glosses, but these aren’t overly sticky. They don’t feel thick or heavy on the lips. They feel nice and thin. They are glosses so they do need re-applied often throughout the day. But, I’m used to that with glosses so it’s not a big deal to me.

The strawberry and grape both have micro glitter in them (mica). I didn’t know that when I got these. None of the product photos showed they had glitter and the description didn’t say it either. I’m not a fan of micro glitter in my lip glosses. I feel once the gloss wears off, it usually leaves behind glitter particles on my lips. Also, they can sometimes feel gritty. So, I was surprised when I saw 2 of the 3 had glitter. Luckily, these didn’t feel gritty. I do notice that there are some glitter particles on my lips after they wear off, but it’s not too bad. The glitter particles are really small, so it’s not really noticeable. So, I don’t mind that.

Overall, these are nice glosses with a nice formula. They might seem pricey when seeing the $30 price tag, but you’re getting 3 tubes of glosses, so that’s only $10 a piece, which isn’t bad. Of course, it isn’t great. You can get a tube of gloss that looks great and works just as well from the drugstore for slightly less. But, the ingredients might make it worth it to spend the little more. I give them 4 stars.

I have used ionizing brushes for over 30 years—since they were first sold by Sharper Image. The negative ions work very well to flatten the surface of the cuticle of each hair, making the hair less likely to break or split, and also softer.

This particular brush works well, but the one I received has a minor design flaw: the brush part pops off so easily that I have to hold it tight with my thumb, making it less ergonomic than it might be... not an issue for me. As for the vibrating part, I couldn't tell, but that's not what I bought it for. This brush generates NO heat, which is exactly what I wanted. Unlike some similar products, there are NO seams that could catch the hair.

TIPS FOR ALL IONIZING BRUSHES:
(1) if they don't need electricity (cord or batteries), they're not the real deal
(2) heating elements, just like heated blow-drying, tend to dry out your hair and make it more brittle: even oily hair can get dried out
(3) brush your hair SLOWLY to get the best result
(4) if your hair is flatter after using it, and you don't like that, bend over and brush it upside down to get more volume

This is what I use as the first step to my night time skin care routine. It is a gentle yet powerful cleansing oil that effectively removes layers of sunscreen, waterproof mascara, liquid eyeliner, liquid glitter eyeshadow, and eyebrow pomade at once. I haven’t tried this with liquid foundation yet, so I cannot say much about it’s ability to remove a full-face make-up.

What I love about it is the texture. It is not a watery nor a heavy type of cleansing oil. It is rather lightweight that easily glides onto the skin for a gentle massage. Two pumps of this cleansing oil is enough to cleanse my entire face thoroughly without leaving any traces of waterproof make-up and sunscreen. It also doesn’t leave any greasy or sticky residue.

My mother told me never to use a brush on wet hair, because wet hair is weaker and more vulnerable to damage than dry hair, and needs the most gentle touch. Well, for years I was faithful to her advice. But then I strayed…

For the past few years, my newest hair stylist has used a brush to comb out my wet tangles. So when I left my trusty Fuller Brush wide tooth comb at a motel, I had only my brush. I figured “Well, my stylist uses a brush and she must know about these things, so I guess mom was just old fashioned.” But as my hair has grown (now at the middle of my back), I’ve been seeing tangles in the brush, even with the best detangling brush around. I was losing too much hair, but not from the roots (which is normal); it appeared to be breaking at some of the tangles, EVEN THOUGH I did not feel any particular “pull” with the brush.

I ordered this comb specifically because of its claims about detangling WET hair, but wasn't expecting much, except for a replacement of my lost comb. But after the first use on my clean damp hair, I saw only a few long and UNTANGLED hairs clinging to it, and they appeared to have come from my head, as in normal. I didn't see any hair that appeared broken or tangled. The combing was QUICK, easy, and completely without frustration. What more could anyone want? Those funny squiggly teeth DO SOMETHING, but how it works is a mystery to me.

I’d recommend this for any adult with medium to long hair, and particularly for CHILDREN who dread the after-shampoo combout.

I had mixed results with these 3 products.  The eye patches are gel patches and not meant to be wet with serum - the serum is released by the gel when it's in contact with skin.  The patches easily stayed in place, but resulted in no visible improvements, and left my undereye area feeling a little dehydrated.  The lip patch is also a gel patch.  It was odd to wear, but it stayed on while I moved around and almost seemed to form a suction seal around my mouth after 10 minutes.  I liked this patch - it left my lips smooth and soft for a day and a half...nice!  The foot booties are for moisturizing only...these are NOT exfoliating booties that take days to work and lead to skin peeling.  They were easy to use and comfortable to wear.  I wore them for 30 minutes and was quite pleased with how soft my feet still felt after 2 days.  My only issue was that after removing the booties I had to spend a good amount of time massaging in the lotion left on my feet...seriously, even after trying to dry them with a towel my feet felt greasy.  Be sure to allow time for the product to absorb afterwards and don't plan to run out the door like I did.  For all of this, I would give the set 4 stars.  However, there's an EXCESSIVE amount of packaging.  The patches all have plastic protectors on both sides, are enclosed in plastic clam shells, and are sealed in the final package.  I felt guiltier than usual when I saw the pile of trash I generated by using this set...these items are definitely over packaged.
